concepts.title: Cell Cycle Phases: Interphase G1 S G2 and M Phase
concepts.definition: The cell cycle runs through interphase, made of G1 phase of growth, S phase of DNA replication and G2 phase of protein synthesis, followed by the M phase of mitosis, and cells that stop dividing enter the quiescent G0 phase.
concepts.key_idea: In a typical human cell of about 24 hours, interphase lasts more than 95 per cent of the cycle while mitosis occupies about an hour.

concepts.title: Mitosis: Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase and Telophase
concepts.definition: Mitosis proceeds through prophase with chromatin condensation and spindle formation, metaphase with chromosomes aligned at the equatorial plate, anaphase with centromere splitting and chromatids moving to poles, and telophase with nuclear envelope reassembly, followed by cytokinesis.
concepts.key_idea: Mitosis conserves the chromosome number of the parent, so it is called equational division, and cytokinesis in plant cells happens by cell plate formation.

concepts.title: Meiosis I and Meiosis II: Synapsis and Crossing Over
concepts.definition: Meiosis involves two successive divisions after one DNA replication: meiosis I with prophase I stages of leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene and diakinesis shows synapsis of homologous chromosomes forming bivalents and crossing over at recombination nodules, and meiosis II resembles mitosis, reducing the chromosome number to half.
concepts.key_idea: Crossing over during pachytene, mediated by the enzyme recombinase, creates genetic variation, and meiosis is called reductional division because the chromosome number halves.
